field.meaning: positive uniform transform factor multiplied by native ramp2732 and XYZ48/52/56
field.abi: No native setter proposed. One validated float32 transaction write; natural next motion update rebuilds matrices.

roles.condition: Use player_roles::Inspect coherence and the existing actor_lifetime generation. The common transform/VM getter has no role exclusion; do not infer readiness from a character number alone.

productPolicyProposal.units: Absolute Actor+60 scalar. The XYZ/ramp product controls actual size.
productPolicyProposal.evidenceStrength: Deliberately small proposed UI policy, not a native clamp or demonstrated safe gameplay range. Separate implementation can choose a stricter subset.

acquireRequirements: Known original build and unchanged relevant native scheduling/transform bodies. Current bridge instance, engine thread, fresh heartbeat and no outstanding ambiguous mutation.

Observer Ready and exact pinned Actor generation; fresh coherent role, current global Actor, STATUS/backlinks/list membership, scene heap/scheduler/map generation and normal game control. Reject pending scene/Drive/rescue/form transition, deleting/frozen/invalid Actor.
Unattached current Actor: decoded Actor+1696==0. Do not use Actor+60 itself or current address as lifetime identity. Save role/form/object binding and native projection context.
No native custom transform callback flag Actor+1736 bit0x08000000. Allow only a verified orientation branch; scalar candidate and original must be finite positive and within disclosed policy.

Initial conservative subset: XYZ48/52/56 and ramp2732 equal native unit values, with stable positive scalar. If allowing nonunit native axes/ramp later, validate them and every compounded operation explicitly; no field writes to normalize them.

Check writable four-byte field span and expected scalar bits immediately before commit. Compute current original and candidate float32 projections from current data, not a stale snapshot. Valid existing world/model matrices alone do not prove every future script/asset is bounded.
projectionRules: Native order is p=f32(ramp*scalar), v[i]=f32(axis[i]*p), then basis-row lane=f32(basisLane*v[i]). Validate each product, not just each input. Fourth vector lane temporarily computes scalar*p but is overwritten with1 before matrix row scaling.

Matrix composition uses all four lanes and f32(f32(f32(m0*x+m1*y)+m2*z)+m3*w). Finite inputs do not prevent overflow/underflow; native normalization also squares and sums XYZ. Reject degenerate/nonfinite intermediates and unsupported custom/attachment paths.

The bounded proposal does not promise all asset deformation, joint indices, child transforms or malicious script values are safe. Attached weapons inherit parent transforms normally; their model/joint data remain native-owned.

scheduling.workerCompletion: 130030 signals context+104 only after queued callbacks return.130130 waits all six wrappers beginning8BB040, stride112, and releases completion tokens before return.
scheduling.integration: Use the existing post-original HookedUpdate/TrainerFrame boundary. Never initiate native transform/motion calls or use a mid-job sample. Native semaphore failures and modified third-party scheduling are outside the proved normal-return contract.

lifetimeAndOwnership.acquire: Capture original scalar bits once, with opaque bridge+Actor generation and mutation identity. Reapplication must never replace the original with a previously applied value.
lifetimeAndOwnership.conflict: If scalar bits differ from the last trainer-owned value, release ownership without overwriting. A same-value native write is invisible to value comparison; this is an explicit limitation, not exclusive ownership.
lifetimeAndOwnership.currentOrRoleChange: Stop applying to the old Actor. Retain its pinned lease only for narrowly validated conditional cleanup, never transfer originals to the replacement Actor. Known retirement is terminal no-write; observer Fault is uncertain and must not be called destruction.
lifetimeAndOwnership.fieldOrControlChange: Stop timer/application on field, scheduler, heap, map, transition or control changes. No stale Actor dereference or release merely because a host timer expired. Deferred cleanup needs a fresh safe native context.
lifetimeAndOwnership.attachmentChange: 3D9FE0/3DA250 preserve scalar60 and alter projection context. A frame-only unattached check cannot prove no attachment interval occurred. Before any restore, validate the saved original against the current transform context. If safety/ownership cannot be established, defer or relinquish explicitly; do not force a baseline under a new parent.
lifetimeAndOwnership.pendingDesign: The product must specify transition handling and test it. Actor generation prevents address reuse, but does not itself observe attachments, native XYZ events, ramp changes or same-value native scalar writes. This research does not introduce a new attachment hook.

collisionPolicy.label: Transform size, with joint/weapon and collision-center consequences; world-collision radii remain unchanged.

World resolver3B9090/16FEC0/1752E0 uses separate Actor1776/1780/1784 values. Floor-alignment3CD220 and joint-derived centers can therefore change even though radii do not.
excludedClaims: No native scripts can change the value

suggestedTests: All three coherent roles and supported forms; forged/mixed role descriptors, zero/malformed scalar, readonly field, pending transition and noncurrent Actor reject without writes.
Bit-exact four-byte commit; native XYZ/ramp/world-radius fields unchanged. Float32 product/sum overflow, underflow/degenerate basis, invalid homogeneous components and native orientation branches.
Acquire/reapply/release idempotence through lost ACK; native scalar conflict; partial write fault journal state; host timeout/disconnect.
Same address reused with a new Actor generation; former Actor still alive after current-player replacement; observer failure distinct from known retirement.
Attach/detach while owned; changed XYZ/ramp while scalar remains trainer-applied; release original under changed context; explicit no-write/deferred terminal outcomes.
Expected worker job callbacks, wait-before-return, modified callback/pin rejection; no direct motion rebuild calls or cross-thread writes.
Collision documentation/readouts retain unscaled radius semantics; no assertion based only on a synthetic fixture that gameplay appearance is correct.
liveValidation: Not performed. No game process, UI, save, product build or product source mutation occurred in this round.
